subject: KaneSharp demo: unexpected latency surge & playbook request
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: KaneSharp demo — sudden latency spike and truncated stream

Morning — quick heads-up from this morning's KaneSharp demo (10:30 PT). During a live streaming walkthrough we observed: 

- Generation latency spiked from ~120ms/token to 1.8s/token for the last 3 minutes of the demo.
- Two streams truncated (client saw "[STREAM CLOSED]" mid-response).
- Datadog traces attached (datadog-traces-20280601-ari.json) show long tail on model-emit and several backpressure spikes on the runtime side.

Repro notes: happens when two concurrent long-session streams (session lengths ~6k tokens) are active and there is a burst of short, high-QPS requests. We saw KV cache eviction events about the same time (kv-evict-heap-snapshot.log).

Ask: Can Platform/Runtime prioritize triage? KaneSharp is mid-PoC and this just happened live — they asked for root cause and mitigation. Leaving logs and a short stdout snippet from their demo.

Thanks — Logan
--
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: KaneSharp demo — sudden latency spike and truncated stream

Ben / Dev — looping you in. KaneSharp (DEAL-3421) hit a significant latency/stream truncation during a live demo. Logan saw KV eviction and sustained tail latencies. They are sensitive to this before we get them past POC sign-off.

What we need: 
1) Immediate mitigations we can flip from Sales/Customer side (route hints, variant fallback, per-demo circuit breaker) to keep demos stable today.
2) Brief triage hypotheses and what logs/ids you need from the customer for a reliable repro.
3) ETA for a hotfix or guardrail (if you have one).

Please reply with a short playbook we can run and I will pass to Ari at KaneSharp.

Sean

Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: KaneSharp demo — sudden latency spike and truncated stream

Thanks for the flags. Initial read (from attached traces + kv snapshot):

- Hypothesis: KV cache churn due to mixing very long sessions (KV footprint large) and high QPS short requests. When eviction happens, runtime incurs high disk/memory ops to repopulate prefix state which amplifies tail latency.
- Secondary contributor: current prefetch policy sometimes races with sticky routing under high concurrency, causing requests to hit cold variants.

Immediate playbook (what Sales can do now):
A. Ask customer to enable "session-sticky-routing" for the demo (no code changes; control plane toggle). This forces long sessions to stick to warm nodes.
B. If available, flip on the "fallback-compat" variant for the demo route (slightly older model binary with lower KV footprint) — reduces latency at slight cost to token quality.
C. Temporary circuit-breaker: set per-route token timeout to 3s for streaming responses to avoid client-observed truncation; will surface a graceful fallback where we return partial response + reason.

What we need from KaneSharp for repro: 
- Full Datadog trace IDs (already attached help; need any missing traces)
- Client request IDs for truncated streams (stdout snippet helps)
- A copy of their demo workload schedule (approx QPS and concurrency)

Short-term fix ETA: we can ship a guarded prefetch-policy patch as a canary in ~48 hours, with a rollback flag. I attached a small patch diff (prefetch-patch-diff.patch) and notes.

I'll take point on the hotfix with Dev on the rollout.

Ben
--
Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Runtime Performance
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: KaneSharp demo — sudden latency spike and truncated stream

Thanks — I can validate Ben's hypothesis. Quick clarifying questions so we don't chase noise: 

1) Can you send two representative request IDs (one truncated stream, one normal) + their full trace IDs? I need exact request IDs to correlate KV eviction events to RPCs.
2) Can we get a pprof of the runtime during the incident window? If customer can't provide, Datadog flamegraph is fine.

Plan (hotfix path):
- Build guarded prefetch backoff: when KV eviction rate exceeds threshold X, temporarily reduce prefetch window and disable aggressive session migration for 1m. This reduces memory churn.
- Canary rollout to 5% of requests for the affected route; monitor latency and truncation rate.
- If canary looks good, ramp to 100% over 4 hours.

ETA: 48 hours for canary-ready patch (assuming we have request IDs and the traces). I'll prepare a runbook for the canary and a rollback.

Dev

Ari — quick update from our side and short-term asks so we can stabilize demos while engineering triages: 

1) Could you share two request IDs from yesterday's demo (one that truncated and one that completed)? Also attach any Datadog trace IDs if you have them.
2) If possible, flip the "session-sticky-routing" toggle for the demo route (this is a control on your Redwood Console under Routing > Overrides). If you'd rather we flip it, reply "please flip" and we'll do it.

Ben and Dev are preparing a guarded prefetch patch and expect a canary-ready drop in ~48 hours once we have the request IDs. We'll run a 5% canary then evaluate.

Thanks for the patience — we want to make sure your next demo is stable.

Sean
